competitors.name: Palermo x Kellanova / Cheez-It
competitors.action: Palermo and Kellanova rolled Cheez-It Frozen Pizza into major U.S. grocers with a Cheez-It-flavored ultra-thin crust and broad initial distribution across Kroger, Ahold, H-E-B, Winn-Dixie, Wegmans, and Food City, with wider expansion planned by August. The signal is that frozen pizza is still attracting attention through licensed snack-brand mashups, not just artisan or health cues.

competitors.name: 7-Eleven / 7-Select
competitors.action: 7-Eleven launched 7-Select Frozen Pizza into freezer doors at participating 7-Eleven, Speedway, and Stripes stores, using the same recipe as its in-store pizza. That is a meaningful channel signal because a major convenience operator is turning its own pizza program into take-home frozen private label instead of keeping pizza only in hot foodservice.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza is gaining momentum through convenience-channel take-home value and attention-grabbing brand mashups
trends.magnitude: Today's clearest signals were Cheez-It using licensed snack equity to win shelf attention and 7-Eleven extending its pizza program into frozen private label, while CSP reported frozen-pizza sales turning around in c-stores.
trends.context: For Real Dough, this means the aisle is not moving in just one premium direction. Big players are widening the category through novelty, convenience, and private-label access points. Real Dough should keep its premium sourdough story sharp, but also stay conscious of where shopper trial is being stolen by simpler, louder hooks.

breaking.headline: The strongest daily read is that frozen pizza growth is widening through convenience and novelty, not just artisan premiumization.
breaking.impact: Cheez-It shows how fast a loud branded hook can earn freezer doors, while 7-Eleven shows c-stores want their own frozen take-home pizza business too. Real Dough should keep its differentiation disciplined and legible: true sourdough, credible quality, and a shelf story that can win without mass-market gimmicks.
